newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-MCFARLANE WINS FOR FIRST TIME.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCFARLANE WINS FOR FIRST TIME.

text.p: Ross McFarlane of Britain shook off his 'journeyman' tag to become the European Tour's fifth first-time winner of the year at the Tournament Players Championship on Sunday.
As gale-force winds at Gut Kaden toughened the challenge, the 36-year-old Englishman won by a shot with a run of three birdies from the 11th after he had double-bogeyed the 10th hole.

He posted a one-under-par 71 for a six-under total of 282 to relegate early leader Gordon Brand Jnr of Scotland to a share of second place with one of the overnight pacesetters, Anders Forsbrand of Sweden.
Brand and Forsbrand shot 72 and 73 respectively.

Finishing joint second with European number one Colin Montgomerie at last year's English Open, behind winner Robert Allenby of Australia, proved to be a key to McFarlane's victory - along with his recovery after the double bogey on the 10th where he drove into a ditch.

"I've often been close but the English Open taught me I could easily be a winner," McFarlane said. "And this time, despite the strong winds, I had a different attitude coming down the last holes, just trying to keep everything as smooth as possible, knowing that if I kept my head the wind was making it difficult for the others to come at me.

"But the 10th gave me a kick up the backside and told me to get my act together, then the key to winning was the four-iron into a howling wind to 10 feet at the 11th, followed by 15 and 25-foot putts at the next two holes."
The other third round leaders, Englishman Howard Clark and Dane Thomas Bjorn, slipped away with rounds of 76 to finish joint ninth.
Forsbrand also double-bogeyed the 10th, when he came up short of the green twice, to lose his chance as he and Brand both missed birdie putts on the last which would have forced a playoff.
"That little putt on the 13th finished me," said Brand. "Putting was my achilles heel all week."
Northern Ireland's Darren Clarke, joint second in last Monday's British PGA, was fourth a further stroke back.

Spain's Miguel Martin made a swing change after his third round 76 and picked up four shots over the last four holes for a 69 and a share of fifth place, leaving him fifth on the Ryder Cup table and almost certain of a place on the team to face the Americans at Valderrama in September.
